roleContext.roleTitle: Field Service Operations Manager, Elevator Maintenance Scheduling
roleContext.jobDescription: Technicians across the northern region are dispatched to elevator maintenance and repair jobs by the scheduling system, and the branches depend on it every working hour. This manager is the person who keeps that dispatching running: primary holder of the dispatch desk's production support rota, first responder when dispatching stops, the coordinator of vendor changes into the live system, the keeper of the response-time figures used in service contract reviews, and the author of the notes that record what the service can and cannot do after each incident. Reports to the regional service director; works daily with the dispatch desk, eleven branches and the vendor's support team.

requirements.text: Keeps the dispatch system dispatching in live operation and is the first responder when a production incident stops dispatching.
Is the primary holder of the dispatch desk's production support rota and the branch escalation route.
Brings vendor changes into the live system through the quarterly change window and records where own checks end and the vendor's begin.
Keeps the dispatch runbook and the response-time figures for service contract reviews current.
Records known limitations and hand-over conditions in the post-incident and change notes.

candidate.originalCvMarkdown:
# Curriculum vitae

Target role: Field Service Operations Manager, Elevator Maintenance Scheduling

## Experience

- Primary holder of the production support rota for the elevator dispatch desk in the northern region from 2021 to 2025, with the branch escalation route running through me during working hours and the duty phone outside them.
- First responder to every production incident that stopped dispatching in those four years; the three vendor outages of 2023 and 2024 are logged under my name in the regional incident log with the vendor's ticket numbers.
- Brought the vendor's scheduling releases into the live system through the quarterly change window, with the change log recording my acceptance checks separately from the vendor's regression checks.
- Kept the dispatch runbook and the response-time figures for the eleven branches current for the service contract reviews, revising the runbook after each incident and each release.
- Wrote the post-incident notes and the release hand-over notes, recording the known limitations of the technician availability feed and what the next rota holder needed to know.

## Work samples

- Work sample: regional incident log extracts for the three vendor outages with the vendor ticket numbers, the change log for the last four quarterly windows and the current dispatch runbook.
